text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2023, the Thandeka Community Care Network deployed 46 trained caregivers across four wards of Mbeluzi District. Caregivers completed 1,284 home visits, an increase of 18% over the previous quarter. Each visit included adherence counselling, a symptom check and a review of the household's medication supply. Volunteers referred twenty-three clients to the Mbeluzi clinic for viral load testing. Stock-outs of cotrimoxazole did not affect any household during the period. However, transport allowances were not paid on time in September, and three caregivers temporarily suspended visits. Supervisors recommend that the allowance schedule be fixed before the next quarter begins.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Kasoro Net Coverage Campaign found that 61,500 long-lasting insecticidal nets were distributed between March and August 2024. Household surveys in twelve sub-counties showed that 72% of children under five slept under a net the night before the interview. Community health promoters registered households door to door before each distribution day. Coverage was lowest in the fishing settlements along Lake Ombere, where many families were not present during registration. The evaluators found no evidence that nets were being resold in local markets. Hang-up visits were planned for every village, but only a third of villages received one. The team recommends that promoters schedule evening visits to reach mobile households.

passages.source_passage: In the quarter ending June 2024, the Saralpur Mother and Child Outreach Project held 38 satellite clinics in villages of Daulatganj block. Auxiliary nurse-midwives registered 412 pregnant women, of whom 64% attended at least three antenatal check-ups. Outreach workers accompanied women to the block hospital when labour began at night. No maternal deaths were recorded in project villages during the quarter. Two newborn deaths occurred, and both families had not received a postnatal home visit within 48 hours. The supply of iron-folic acid tablets was adequate, but weighing scales were broken at five clinic sites. The team will replace the scales before the monsoon season closes rural roads.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation reviews the first eighteen months of the Pelangi Coast Early Warning Programme, which covers 27 fishing villages on the Teluk Sari shoreline. By December 2023, volunteer warning teams had been formed in 25 villages, and each team had received a siren, a radio and a printed evacuation map. Trained volunteers briefed school teachers on evacuation routes in every village. During the October cyclone drill, 81% of registered households reached a designated shelter within 30 minutes. Older residents with limited mobility were not included in the household register in several villages. The evaluators also noted that radio messages were never translated into the Bajau dialect. Village chiefs strongly support the programme, and two district councils have pledged matching funds for shelter repairs.

passages.source_passage: Volunteer Guide, Session 4: Choosing Drought-Tolerant Seed. In this session you will help farmers in the Ruvanda Hills compare three sorghum varieties tested by the Green Furrow Trust since 2021. Begin by asking each farmer how many weeks their maize crop survived without rain last season. Explain that the Kibo-2 variety needs about 90 days to mature, roughly a month less than local maize. Do not promise farmers that any variety will survive a year of total crop failure. Farmers should plant at least half an acre with the new seed so that the comparison is fair. Groups should have no more than 25 members, because larger groups make the field demonstration hard to follow.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Nyakoro Savings for Change Programme covered 140 village savings and loan groups formed since January 2022. Members had saved a combined 38.4 million shillings by the end of the second cycle, and 87% of groups had shared out their funds as planned. Women make up seventy percent of members and hold most chair positions. Loan repayment was strong, with fewer than 4% of loans more than a month overdue. However, groups in Lokiri sub-county did not keep written records after the field officer left. Evaluators recommend that literate members train group secretaries in simple bookkeeping before the third cycle begins.

passages.source_passage: Annual Report to the Halvorsen Justice Fund, 2023. Over the year, the Mbarali Paralegal Network trained 32 community paralegals and opened advice desks in nine rural markets. Paralegals handled 2,310 cases, most involving land boundaries, inheritance and unpaid wages. Just over 40% of cases were resolved through mediation without going to court. Widows who had been evicted by relatives were helped to reclaim their homes in 57 cases. The network did not take on criminal defence work, which remains outside its mandate. Funding for paralegal stipends was not renewed by the district council in July, so the network covered the shortfall from reserves. We ask the Fund to consider a two-year grant from 2024.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring visits in May 2024 covered all 18 boreholes drilled by the Clearspring Rural Water Initiative in Ondoro and Mapesi wards. Fifteen boreholes were functioning, and average queuing time at the pump had fallen to about 12 minutes. Water committees collect a monthly fee of 500 shillings per household for repairs. Women chair seven of the committees, and men chair the rest. Three boreholes were not working because spare parts had not arrived from the district store. Household latrine coverage rose to 68%, up from 41% at baseline. Handwashing stations were present beside most new latrines, but soap was seen at fewer than half of them. Committees have never received refresher training on pump maintenance since the project began.

passages.source_passage: Trainer's Note, Module 2: Opening a Protection Case. This module prepares volunteers in Block C of Haradi Camp to support caseworkers from the Safe Passage Refugee Council. Allow about 45 minutes for the role-play and ten minutes for questions. Remind volunteers that they must never ask a survivor to describe an assault in detail. Volunteers record only the person's name, shelter number and the type of help requested. Caseworkers, not volunteers, decide whether a case is urgent. In 2023, roughly one in five referrals reached a caseworker after more than 72 hours, so volunteers should hand forms to the duty caseworker before leaving the block each day.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the April to September 2024 season for the Lusindi Farmer Field School Network. Facilitators ran 54 field schools, each with a demonstration plot comparing mulched and unmulched beans. Attendance averaged 22 farmers per session, and 58% of participants were women. In the mulched plots, bean yields were about one third higher than in the control plots. Extension officers trained lead farmers in compost making at the Chilala demonstration site. Pest scouting was not practised regularly in Mweru zone, where no facilitator was assigned after June. The network has not yet confirmed whether seed vouchers will be available next season.
